reasons: Rule correctly applied: the Agreement contains no insurance provision, and Commerce One is a hosting/professional-services vendor (on-site consultant, MarketSite.net Service handling Corio and Customer data), so an insert is warranted under the detection guidance.
Direction is correct — the obligation is placed on the counterparty (Commerce One) in favor of Corio, our client.

Inserted covenant tracks the preferred position and model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where data is processed, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request, term plus one year) with no unnecessary changes to existing text; p0132 is left unaltered.
Placement in the Miscellaneous section after 14.9 matches the redline guidance; the duplicate 14.10 numbering is expressly flagged for renumbering in the comment, so it is not a substantive defect.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position and offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback; severity 'low' is consistent with the rule.
